intro: I wanted a game engine where I could follow an idea all the way through, understand what was happening underneath, and change the parts that annoyed me. So I started building one.
dataTitle: Make it once. Know where it goes.
dataParagraphs: Blender’s datablocks made a lot of sense to me. A mesh, material, or behavior should be something I can reuse, with a clear relationship between the original and everywhere it’s used.

In Plush, I can change a shared object and have that change reach its uses, while still choosing what varies locally. The graph shows those connections. Bundles let me take useful work into another project. I want to spend less time wondering which copy of something I’m editing.
stackIntro: C# for the engine and gameplay, Python for authoring and automation. I like having ordinary code I can read and tools I can change.
stack: Separate runtime; no editor or Python
extras: MCP tools let an assistant inspect the project and help with setup or scripts. I’m using AI extensively to build Plush, but I want to make games in it without needing an agent to operate it.
Room for the things I enjoy
There’s a music tracker in the editor, too. I’ve used trackers for years, and wanted patterns, instruments, and the game in the same place.
closing: It’s still in development. I’m building it to use it, break things, figure out why they broke, and keep making it better.
